title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from this page and its neighbours). The page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' block, which studies the arithmetic fundamental group of the modular curve / moduli stack M_{1,1} over Q together with its λ-line cover.

Notation, as I read it:
- 𝔊^{+∧} is the profinite completion of SL2(Z), the geometric fundamental group of M_{1,1}. Ĝ is the version including orientation-reversing elements (reflections τ, τ').
- M is the arithmetic fundamental group, an extension 1 → 𝔊^{+∧} → M → Π_Q^~ → 1 (previous page, (4 bis)).
- π ⊂ 𝔊^{+∧} is the completed principal congruence subgroup Γ(2)^. π_0 is the profinite free group on two generators, π_1^geom of P^1−{0,1,∞}, with π = π_0 × μ and μ = {±1}.
- M → S_3 is the action on 2-torsion, i.e. on the cusps of the λ-line.
- M(0) is the Galois section at the tangential base point λ = 0 (a cusp).
- σ (= i) and ρ (= e^{2πi/3}) are the elliptic points. Their stabilizers are L_σ ≅ Z/4 and L_ρ ≅ Z/6.
- N*_x is the subgroup of M sending x to x^{±} (normalizer of the stabilizer, up to the sign character).

(8): M^!_0 = M(0)·π_0 is the arithmetic π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}. It sits inside M^! = M(0)·π = Ker(M → S_3), the arithmetic π_1 of the λ-line stack. Because ±1 is central, M^! ≅ M^!_0 × μ.

(9)–(10): Define M(1/2) := N*_σ ∩ M^!_0. The projection M → γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Π_Q^~ restricts to an isomorphism M(1/2) ≅ γ_{ρ,σ}. So M(1/2) is the image of a Galois section of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}/Q). By the notation it is the section attached to the rational point λ = 1/2, which lies over j = 1728 and is the fixed point of λ ↦ 1−λ. That is, it is the decomposition group at the CM point σ, lifted to the λ-line.

(11): One gets semidirect-product splittings:
- M ≅ M(1/2)·𝔊^{+∧}
- M^! ≅ M(1/2)·π
- M^!_0 ≅ M(1/2)·π_0
- N*^!_σ ≅ M(1/2) × μ
- N*_σ ≅ M(1/2)·L_σ

(12) restates the inverse isomorphism γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ M(1/2) ⊂ N*_σ.

(c), (13)–(14): The same analysis begins for ρ. N*_ρ = {u : u(ρ) = ρ^{ε_3(u)}}, where ε_3 is the mod-3 cyclotomic sign character. Its intersections are:
- with Ĝ: the dihedral group D_ρ = {1,τ'}·L_ρ;
- with 𝔊: L_ρ ≅ Z/6;
- with π: μ;
- with π_0: {1}.

The next page continues: N*_ρ ∩ M^!_0 = M'(−j), the decomposition group at λ = −j (a primitive sixth root of unity over j = 0). It is isomorphic to the index-2 subgroup {ε_3 = 1}, i.e. essentially Γ_{Q(√−3)}.

Purpose: to describe explicitly the Galois sections ('decomposition groups') at the two CM points j = 1728 and j = 0. These serve as auxiliary base points for writing the Galois / Grothendieck–Teichmüller action ('équation des lacets') with respect to the elliptic points, not only the cusp.
errors: Small gaps rather than errors. The claimed intersections, e.g. N*_σ ∩ 𝔊^{+∧} = L_σ (normalizer of a finite elliptic subgroup in profinite SL2(Z) equals itself) and N*_σ ∩ π_0 = {1}, are asserted without proof. In the profinite setting they need an argument: the normalizer of finite subgroups of a profinite free product (Herfort–Ribes type results). They are true.
The isomorphism (10) presupposes that N*_σ ∩ M^!_0 surjects onto γ_{ρ,σ}, i.e. that the rational point λ = 1/2 really lies in the M^!-orbit compatible with σ. This is fine, but it is implicit.

ideas.what: Decomposition group / Galois section of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}/Q) at the rational point λ = 1/2 (over j = 1728), realized as the normalizer of the elliptic stabilizer of order 4 intersected with the λ-line group.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition groups at rational (CM) points; Galois sections of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} and of the λ-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura and others (1990s work on Galois actions on profinite modular / braid groups and on rational-point sections of P^1−{0,1,∞})

ideas.what: Semidirect-product splittings of the arithmetic π_1 of M_{1,1}, of the λ-line, and of P^1−{0,1,∞} using the CM section instead of a tangential base point at a cusp.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the fundamental exact sequence by a rational-point section

ideas.what: Analogous treatment at j = 0 / λ = −j, where the section is defined only over the kernel of the mod-3 cyclotomic character ε_3, i.e. over Q(√−3).
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition group at a CM point defined over Q(ζ_3)

missed.claim: Explicit evidence that Grothendieck systematically used the CM points j = 1728 (λ = 1/2) and j = 0 (λ = −j) as base points for Galois sections in his study of the Galois action on profinite SL2(Z), alongside tangential base points at cusps. This anticipates later uses of λ = 1/2 and λ = −ω in GT-type computations.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that the 'elliptic point' sections, later used by Nakamura and others, were part of Grothendieck's setup. It is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard bookkeeping of normalizers and Galois sections at CM points in the arithmetic π_1 of M_{1,1}. The content is known to specialists. Only the historical anticipation is of mild interest.
transcription_corrections: 'M^\natural ≃ M(1/2).𝔖^{+∧}' in (11) should read approximately 'M ≃ M(1/2).𝔊^{+∧}' (gothic G for profinite SL2(Z)); this is consistent with the extension in (4 bis).
The page header '515' is Grothendieck's own page number; the archive page is 622.
'd'où[?] ... des scindages en produits semi-directs[?]' is consistent with the next page's 'd'où on déduit des scindages en produits semi-directs'.
In (13), the parenthetical '(= ε_3[τ'](ρ))' is written below the formula as a gloss on ρ^{ε_3(u)}.
